items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the tax law, in relation to credits for premiums paid for long-term care insurance policies
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5230

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the tax law, in relation to credits
for premiums paid for long-term care insurance policies

PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:  The purpose of this bill is to
expand upon the provisions of Chapter.  563 of the Laws of 2010 and
Chapter 465 of the Laws of 2014, which expanded the types of end of
life care that can be financed by an accelerated death benefit rider
attached to a life insurance policy. Under these new laws, persons who
have resided in a nursing home for three months or more or require end
of life or palliative care for three months or more at a residential,
health care facility, receive home care services or hospice care and
such services are expected to be needed until death can now be
financed by a life insurance policy rider. This bill expands the
current tax credit inducements that exist for the purchase of long
term care insurance to also include these new life insurance policy
riders.

SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Amends Tax Law section 190 to expand the tax credit for
purchasing long term care insurance (20% of the premium paid) to
include a policy rider to a life insurance policy (30% of the premium
paid for such rider)that provides for long term care-like coverages.
The reason for this expansion is because, under new laws recently
adopted in New York, the life insurance rider to pay accelerated
benefits for end of life care covers the same types of end of life
care covered under long term care insurance.

Section 2: Amends Tax Law section 210-B to expand the tax credit
incentives currently used to encourage the purchase long term care
insurance (20% of the premium paid)to include premiums paid to
purchase life insurance riders (30% of the premium paid for such
riders)that cover similar end of life expenses as it relates to the
corporate franchise rate.

Section 3: Amends Tax Law section 606 to add the LTC (long term
care)life insurance policy rider premiums paid that is eligible for a
tax credit, in addition the tax credit that is currently available for
long term care insurance for personnel income tax calculations.

Section 4: Amends Tax Law section 1511 to add the LTC tax credit for
the purchase of life insurance policy riders for insurance corporation
taxes.

JUSTIFICATION:  As the general population becomes older, more and more
individuals are looking for affordable ways to finance their nursing
home and long term care needs. While there are available policies that
provide payment for long term care, more products should be authorized
under New York law so that consumers will have more types of insurance
coverage available to meet their specific needs or the needs of their
family.  This can be done by encouraging more younger persons to
obtain such coverage and incentivize more life insurers to offer such
coverages.  By both encouraging persons to purchase such policies and
incentivizing carriers to offer such policy riders, this should
greatly expand the number of covered lives protected.


In addition, encouraging more individuals to finance their own long
term care, will help to curtail future expenditures from the State's
Medicaid program, which currently finances the lion's share of the
provision of long term care in this State. This bill is a further
extension of new laws such as Chapter 563 of the Laws of 2010 and
Chapter 465 of the Laws of 2014 which are geared towards encouraging
individuals to finance their own long term care and nursing home care
as we all get older via life insurance policy riders.

The reason for the enhanced 30% tax credit for the rider (as opposed
to the 20% tax credit for long term care insurance) is because the
cost of these riders is considerably lower than the cost of LTC
insurance, hence as a percentage of money paid cost of such subsidy
should be about the same.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY: New bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:  It is the intent of this bill encourage the
increased use: of Long Term Care insurance and policy riders to life
insurance policies for the use as a financing mechanism to finance end
of life care. This, in the end, should help to decrease State Medicaid
expenditures.

EFFECTIVE DATE: This act shall take effect on April, 1st of the year
next succeeding its date of enactment.

items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No. 268

TO THE SENATE:

I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill:

Senate Bill Number 5230-A, entitled:

    "AN  ACT  to  amend the tax law, in relation to credits for premiums
      paid for long-term care insurance policies"

    NOT APPROVED

  This bill would expand the  current  tax  credit  for  long-term  care
insurance  premiums  to  include premiums paid for life insurance policy
riders that allow the option of using a portion of eventual death  bene-
fits to pay for end-of-life long-term care.

  While  long-term  care  insurance is an important financing option for
many people, this bill is problematic for two reasons. First,  Insurance
Law  Section  1117(g) mandates that in order to qualify for a tax credit
on long-term care insurance premiums, the life  insurance  policy  rider
must be approved by the Superintendent of Insurance using certain stand-
ards  pertaining to long-term care. Because life insurance policy riders
do not meet these standards, the Superintendent  is  unable  to  approve
them  for  the  tax credit. Second, the proposed tax credit would have a
significant  fiscal  impact  to  the  State,  and  should  therefore  be
addressed  in  the  context of the upcoming State budget negotiations. I
look forward to discussing how to best accomplish the  policy  goals  of
this bill with the Legislature.

  The bill is disapproved.                    (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
